overall_reason: The copy and the product views are specific to one webhook product (typed Stripe handler, per-attempt backoff log, a replay command with a matched/delivered count), but they sit on a stock dev-tool skeleton (mock hero, logo strip, numbered 4-step row, zig-zag splits, unsourced stat band, three tiers, CTA band) in the near-black plus one-lime-accent look nobody justified.

findings.evidence: T-STOCK-ORDER: hero with product mock (code editor + event log) -> logo strip ("Works with any HTTP sender, including stripe github shopify ...") -> numbered 1-2-3-4 steps (Receive / Type / Deliver / Replay) -> two alternating text/visual splits -> stat band (99.99% / < 50 ms / 0 / 4 regions) -> three pricing tiers (Free / Pro $49 / Scale Custom) -> closing CTA band ("Get an endpoint in a minute") -> footer. Six stock sections in stock order, which caps the read at mixed.
findings.before: mock hero, strip, 4 steps, zig-zag, stats, 3 tiers, CTA band
findings.after: Keep the strongest specific artefact (the replay terminal with 1,842 matched / delivered) as the page's spine and cut the stat band and CTA band; the hero already ends with an install command, so the closing band repeats it
findings.why: Specific words on a default skeleton still read as a default page; a neighbouring dev-tool brief would get this exact sequence.

findings.evidence: Visible dark-single-accent cluster: near-black ground, one saturated lime used for the primary buttons, the headline second line "Typed events", bullets, check marks and the Pro card border; monospace on non-code labels ("stream live", "terminal", "relay cli 2.4", the sender strip, step numbers "01"-"04"). T-MIRROR: Vercel/Linear/Resend-adjacent pages ship this hero and nav.
findings.after: Name a reason for the look or change one axis, e.g. set labels in the text face and keep mono only for real code and payloads
findings.why: A look family chosen without a reason counts against 'made' even when the content is specific.

findings.evidence: "99.99% ingest uptime, last 12 months", "< 50 ms p95 receive to deliver", "0 events dropped after ack", "4 regions" with no source, status-page link or as-of date. "0 events dropped" cannot be falsified from the page.
findings.after: Link the uptime figure to the status page with an as-of date ([DATA NEEDED: status URL]); replace "0 events dropped" with the guarantee it implies ("at-least-once delivery after ack"), which the page already states
findings.why: An unsourced four-figure band is the most recognisable proof-by-number habit; this page's evidence is stronger in its terminal views.

findings.evidence: Pill "New  Replay by time range or event ID" above the headline. T-EYEBROW/T-DELETION: the same feature is the subject of the "Replay without asking the provider" section, so the pill adds nothing the page does not say later.
findings.before: "New · Replay by time range or event ID" pill
findings.after: Remove the pill; if replay is the launch, make it the hero's sub-line
findings.why: A version/news pill over the hero is template furniture.

findings.where: "Retries that respect your downstream" and "Replay without asking the provider", tiles 00-01
findings.evidence: Text-left/visual-right then visual-left/text-right, each with three lime-bulleted lines: a mirrored zig-zag pair. The delivery-attempts panel draws a dot on an unlabeled track per attempt; the dot position has no axis or scale, so T-DELETION removes it with no loss (the 503/503/timeout/200 column carries the meaning).
findings.after: Put both mechanisms in one section with one shared panel (attempt, wait, status as a table), or keep the panel and drop the tracks
findings.why: Alternating splits are the stock way to fill the middle of a page; the faux chart is decoration in a data costume.

strengths: Headline and sub-line say what it is and for whom in one screen: "Webhooks in. Typed events out." plus validation, retries and replay; it passes T-FIVE-SECOND.

Product views carry real, internally consistent detail: retries: 8 with exponential backoff, "backoff 2s, 8s, 32s ... delivered after 42.6s", the replay command with 1,842 matched and 1,842 delivered.
Each step card carries a concrete artefact (POST /in/src_8fk2/stripe, relay gen --lang ts, at-least-once ordered per key, relay replay --since 2h).
Pricing explains its unit honestly: "An event is one accepted webhook. Retries and replays are not billed."
The sender strip is plain text ("Works with any HTTP sender, including") rather than a fake customer logo wall.
not_investigated: Image-only item: no DOM, no mechanical sweep; look-family tells judged by eye, not measured.
Truth of the stated metrics and prices: no supplied facts.
